basis: Prenatal alcohol exposure causes defining CNS dysfunction and neurodevelopmental impairment; growth deficiency and facial features do not establish additional organ damage.
Malignant notochordal tumor arising in the axial skeleton; neurologic invasion or compression is not established as common across all sites.
Embryonal malignancy arising in the supratentorial brain.
Inflammation damages retina and optic nerve through infection or immune activation; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis.
Inherited retinal cone degeneration; no established extraocular involvement.
Functioning pituitary gonadotroph tumor; compressive visual impairment and visual field defects occur in 30-79%. Other neurologic complications are occasional.
Thoracic and limb skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia with respiratory dysfunction is common (>30%). Renal and hepatic disease vary substantially by subtype.
Adenocarcinoma originates in the seminal vesicle, a reproductive organ outside the axes; no common direct involvement of another axis is established.
Postinfectious brain inflammation, commonly mediated by an immune response; no additional organ injury defines the umbrella.
Hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, hepatic injury and systemic microangiopathy define HELLP; renal glomerular injury with proteinuria occurs in 30-79%; acute kidney injury is uncommon.
Primary CNS neoplasm of pineal parenchymal cells; the pineal gland is also an endocrine organ.
Defining external-ear malformation and middle-ear ossicular abnormalities cause conductive hearing loss; micrognathia alone does not establish additional functional damage.
Name and consistent eye-infection ancestry identify parasitic intraocular infection; the definition's reference to epicondyles appears erroneous.
Ependymal CNS tumor, commonly arising in the spinal cord.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are principal features; reported cardiac, ocular, thyroid and esophageal defects lack evidence of frequency above 30%.
Loss of coordinated bladder and urethral sphincter function; an underlying neurologic disease is a separate condition rather than damage caused by dyssynergia.
Pulmonary valve stenosis and cafe-au-lait lesions define Watson syndrome; developmental delay and pectus carinatum each occur in 2/3 reported patients; Lisch nodules are non-damaging.
Childhood myelodysplastic neoplasm causing persistent cytopenia and abnormal marrow hematopoiesis.
Benign neoplasm originating in cutaneous sweat glands; labels reflect the usual sites across the umbrella.
Granulomatous endometrial inflammation caused by infection or immune-mediated disease such as sarcoidosis; the reproductive site itself has no axis.
Intellectual disability defines the syndrome; pyloric stenosis and blepharophimosis occur in 80-99%, finger/foot malformations in 30-79%; cardiac defects are below 30%.
Autoinflammatory periodic fever syndrome; recurrent fever alone does not establish damage to another organ.
Neonatal thyroid hormone excess is most commonly caused by transferred maternal thyroid-stimulating antibodies; tachycardia alone does not establish cardiac damage.
Generalized skeletal dysplasia with bowing, osteopenia and contractures; atrial septal defect occurs in 1/3. Hepatomegaly in 1/3 lacks demonstrated hepatic dysfunction.
Infection directly inflames and damages the posterior uvea and adjacent ocular tissues.
